body.x: UStation Inc. (CEO Baek Junho) announced its participation in CES 2025 in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 at the K-Startup Pavilion.

UStation specializes in developing portable electrocardiograms, blood pressure monitors, and AIoT medical devices with biosensors. The company has leveraged its material components and measurement solutions expertise to create a data platform that integrates measurement instruments with medical devices, solidifying its competitiveness in the healthcare industry.

At CES 2025, UStation will present its portable electrocardiogram device. Designed for ease of use, the device enables users to independently monitor their heart rate without assistance from medical professionals or caregivers. It quickly detects abnormalities in heart rate data, supporting early arrhythmia diagnosis.
The device maximizes portability, allowing users to frequently monitor their heart rate by placing their finger on it. Its user-friendly operation makes it accessible to a broad audience.

body.cap: UStation’s portable electrocardiogram devices | Photo provided by UStation

body.x: The device connects seamlessly to a mobile application, providing an intuitive way to view measurement data. The device includes a built-in LCD screen that directly displays heart rate data for users who struggle with apps or separate displays. UStation aims to introduce this solution to global healthcare stakeholders, promoting user-driven health management and exploring new market opportunities.

A UStation representative stated, “We decided to participate in CES 2025 to achieve global market expansion with our portable electrocardiogram device, which enables anyone to monitor their heart rate anytime, anywhere easily. Following regulatory approval and distribution efforts in Vietnam, we are pursuing FDA approval to enter the North American market.”

The representative added, “After a successful promotion at CES and FDA approval, we plan to supply our portable electrocardiogram devices to North America and other global markets. Additionally, we are accelerating the development of a medical thermal imaging camera solution, building on our existing thermal imaging technology, further to expand our product lineup in the healthcare sector.”

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
